comments.value:
Now that there's a whole discourse about garbage worlds flooding the platform I think this is a good alternative to the like/dislike system that VRChat has proposed. I've got some ideas for this as well.

You should be able to let anybody make a curator page of sorts, whether it's about their personal recommendations or something themed ("underrated liminal worlds" or "horror hangout worlds" for example) and let them leave a positive review, a neutral 'informative' review or a negative review.

Curators should have no impact on the discovery algorithm unless someone is subscribed to them. If they are subscribed to some, they should be able to see worlds that have been recommended by the curators they follow more often and worlds that have been given negative reviews by their subscribed curators will be hidden. This should make all camps happy, since this way people get to choose which curators they trust with their judgment.

Some benefits about this system:

- It doesn't suffer from the "definition of AI" problem that VRChat has pointed out (where no combination of AI usage for a concrete definition has gotten more than 10% agreement from the community) because people get to choose who they follow (curator who only gives negative reviews to sloppy AI spam worlds vs. curator who negatively reviews all worlds with any evidence of AI usage).

- The system is entirely human-driven with the only computer influence being an algorithm deciding how recommendations from your subscribed curators affect your feed.

- It's opt-in so people who dislike the system can ignore it entirely and it will have no influence on their feed by default.

- The curator system is a tried and true system that Steam has been using for many years now.

The problem with the like/dislike system is that it's easy for something to be dislike-bombed due to e.g. a creator having shared a controversial opinion as opposed to a world actually being judged for its quality. Steam has mitigations for those kinds of things by disqualifying unjust review bombs on store pages but it would be far too much to handle for VRChat's team with the countless worlds that pop up in VRChat.

details:
Like how Steam has curators you can follow to see the games they recommend, I think it would be great if VRChat allowed you to follow community curators to see the worlds they recommend. Open up a person's curator page and you'd get a window much like the current Worlds panel but featuring exclusively the worlds that person recommends. They could even categorize them by type. Experiences, Social Spaces, Homes, etcetera.

Curators could even write brief reviews or descriptions of the worlds in their lists.

Maybe we could upvote the curators whose recommendations we find useful?

 Honestly, I'd just wholesale steal the curator idea directly from Steam and apply it to VRChat.

This could be much more useful for finding content in VRChat than waiting for a random YouTube creator to post some world recommendations. The easier it is for users to find worlds that really appeal to them, the more engaged they become with VRChat in general.
title: World Curators
